Notification No. S.R.O. 299(1)/2001, dated 10th May, 2001..- In exer~ise of the powers conferred by clause (b) of section 43 of the Seclfrities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan Act, 1997 (XLII of 199j), reac\ with section 5A of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 (XVII of 1969), the Securities and Exchange Commission of Paklstan, with the approval of the Federal Government, hereby makes the following rules, namely:- '1. Short title and commencement.- (1) These rules may be called the Brokers and Agents Registration Rules, 2001. ~2) They shall come into force at once. 2. Definitions.- (1) In these rules, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,- !(a) "4ct" means the Securities and Exchange Commission of , P~kistan Act, 1997 (XLII of 1997); III -95 ~ -.; ;; :~::~,.: III- 96 R. 2(1)(b) Company Law and Procedures (b) "clearing house" means a clearing house of a stock exchange performing the- function of clearing and settling trades in securities or a clearing company established for such purpose; (c) "Commission" means the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan; (d) "Enquiry officer" means any officer of the Commission, or any other person, who is appointed by the Commission under the Ordinance or the Act; (e) "Ordinance" means the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 (XVII of 1969); (f) "Regulations" means the regulations made by a Stock Exchange; and (g) "Schedule" means the Schedule annexed to these rules. (2) All other words and expressions used but not defined in these rules shall have the same meaning as are assigned to them in the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan Act, 1997 (XLII of 1997), and the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 (XVII of 1969). 3. Application for registration.~ (1) A member desirous of acting !ilS a broker shall make an application to the Commission in Form A as set out in the First Schedule, for grant of a certificate of registration through the stock exchange of which he is a member. (2) An application for registration \lnder sub-rule (1) shall be submitted alongwith fee as prescribed in the Second Schedule. (3) The brokers who are working as broker before coming into force of these rules, shall apply for registration in accordance with the provisions of sub-rule (1), within ninety days of the date of coming into force of these rules. (4) The stock exchange shall forward the application to the Commission within fourteen days from the date of its receipt. 4. Eligibility for regi~tration.- (1) A person shall be eligible for registration as a broker under these rules, if he- (a) is a member of the stock exchange; (b) is not less than twenty-one years of age; (c) is a citizen of Pa~istan; (d) has atleast passed graduation or equivalent examination from an institution recognized by the Governm~nt: Provided that the Commission may relax the educational qualification in suitable eases on merit having regard to the applicants experience; III -97 BrQkers anq Agents Reg. Rules, 2001 R. 5(6) (e) ~s not a lunatic or a person of unsound mind; (f)las not been convicted of an offence involving fraud or breach of rust; (g) as not been adjudicated as insolvent or has suspended payment r has compounded with his creditors; . (h) has experience of not less than five years in the business of ~uying, selling or dealing in securities; (i) taS not been a partner of a brokerage firm or a diI;ector of a rokerage company which has been convicted of an offence oncerning brokerage; I G) has not defaulted in payment of dues at a clearing hou~e; (k) ~as not defaulted in compliance with the provisidns of the 'i rrdinance, the Act and the rules and regulaticpns made thereunder; (1) ~s not in default on settlement of an investor complaint where I such complaint has been adjudicated by a stock exchange or a II fommittee of a stock exchange or the Commission; and j (m) pas complied with the directives of the Commission in respect of I tUSiness conduct, dealings with clients and financial prudence. (2) he applicant shall remain in compliance with the requirements of !sub-ru e (1) at all times and inform the Commission immediately when he! is non compliailt with any of the terms and conditions. (2) irhe certificate of registration of a broker shall be valid for one year. (3) ['he Commission shall send an intimation of registration under s~b-rule ~1) to the concerned stock exchange or stock exchanges. (6) applicant aggrieved by the decision of the Commission under sub-rule (5) may apply, within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such intimation, to the Commission for review of its decision.~ 111- 98 R.6 Company Law and Procedures 6. Effect of refusal for registration. -A person whose application for grant of a certificate of registration as a broker has been refused by the Commission from and on the date of receipt of the decision under sub-rule (5) of rule 5 shall not deal in securities as a broker. 7. Renewal of registration.- (1) The certificate of registration shall be renewable on payment of fee as prescribed in the Second Schedule. (2) Requirements of these rules as applicable to initial registration shall also apply to renewal of the registration. 8. Suspension of registration.- Where the Commission is of the opinion that a broker- (i) 'has failed to remain in compliance with any conditions subject to which certificate of registration was granted under these rules; (ii) 'has otherwise failed to comply with any requirement of the Act ~or the Ordinance or of any rules or direction made or given Jthereunder; , (iii) has contravened the rules and regulations of the stock exchange; (iv) has failed to follow any requirement of the code of conduct laid down in the Thirq Schedule; (v) has failed to comply with the directives of the Commission in respect of business conduct, dealings with clients and financial prudence; (vi) has failed to finish any information related to his transactions in securities as may be required by the Commission: (vii) has failed to submit periodical returns as required by the Commission; (viii) has furnished wrong or false information; (ix) has failed to settle an investor complaint where such complaint had been adjudicated by a stock exchange or a committee of a stock exchange or the Commission; (x) has not co-operated in any enquiry or inspection conducted by the Commission;, (xi) has indulged in manipulating price rigging or cornering activities in a stock exchange; (xii) his financial position has deteriorated to such an extent that the Commission is of the opinion that his continuance in securities business shall not be in the interest of investors; and (xiii) has been suspended by a stock exchange, II the Commission may, if it considers necessary in the public interest so to I do, by order in writing:- 111-99 Brokers and Agents Reg. Rules. 2001 R.ll (a) $uspend the registration of a broker for such period as may be ~pecified in the order; or (b) impose on a broker a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees: I Prov~ded that an appropriate opportunity of being heard shall be provided fto the broker to clarify his position with regard to suspension of registrat~on. 9. Cancellation of registration.- Where the Commission is of the oPini'lon that the cause of suspension of registration under rule 8 continue during the period of such suspension, or a broker whose re~istrat 'on has been suspendedr (i) ~s engaged in insider trading; I (ii) bas been found guilty of fraud, or convicted of a criminal offence; 1 (iii) ~as his membership cancelled by a stock exchange; or 1 (iv) ~as not complied with a directive of the Commission, the Commission may, if it considers it necessary for the protection of investor~ so to do, by order in writing, cancel the regis~ration of the broker: I Provided that no such order shall be made except after giving the broker a~ opportunity of being heard. . 10. (f) Iis wound up by an order passed by a Court. j (2) Where a certificate of registration stands cancelled under subrule (I)' tlthe concerned stock exchange or clearing house shall intimate the Commis ion immediately about such cancellation of the certificate of registra ion. 11.11 Broker, etc., to clear liabilities.- Notwithstanding the refusal, suspensation or cancellation of a certificate of registration under rules 6, 8, 9 or 10, the l)roker shall be responsible for clearing all his obligati ns up to the date on which he has been working as such broker. 111- 100 R.12 Company Law and Procedures ) 12. Brokers to abide by code of conduct.- A broker holding a certificate of registration under these rules shall abide by the code of conduct specified in the Third Schedule. 13. Application for registration of agent.- (1) A person desirous of acting as an agent shall make an application to the Commission in Form C as set out in First Schedule, for grant of a certificate of registra,tion, through a broker with whom he is to be affiliated and the concern~d stock exchange. (2) ,JThe application for registration under sub-rule (1) I;hall be accompanied by an authority letter from a broker with whom he is tq be affiliated alongwith two references including one from his banker, (3) The application shall b~ submitted alongwith fee as prescribed in the Second Schedule. (4) The stock exchange on receipt of an application under ;;ub-rule (1) shall verify the information contained therein and shall alsl) certify that the applicant is eligible for registration as per criteria spel:ified in sub-rule (5). (5) The eligibility criteria for registration as an agent shall be as specified in rule 3 of the Member's Agents and Traders (Eligibility Standards) Rules, 2001. (6) The stock exchange shall forward the application form, alongwith their recommendations, of such applicants who comply vrith the requirements aforesaid, to the Commission within thirty days from the date of its receipt. 14. Registration.- (1) The Commission, if it is satisfied tllat the applicant is eligible for registration as an agent, shall grant a cer~ificate of registration to the applicant in Form D as set out in the First Scl.\edule, subject to such conditions, as it may deem fit. (2) The certificate of registration shall be valid for one year. (3) No application made under sub-rule (1) of rule 13 shall be refused except after giving the applicant a reasonable opportunity of being heard. (4) In case the Commission refuses the grant of certificate of registration to an applicant after providing the opportunity of being heard under sub-rule (2), the decision shall be communicated to the applicant as well as the member and the stock exchange concerned within fourteen days of the last hearing given to the applicant, stating therein the grounds for refusal. (5) ,An applicant aggrieved by the decision of the Commission under sub-rule.(4), may apply, within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such intimation, to the Commission for review of its decision. Integrity.- A broker shall maintain high standards of integrity, promptitude and fairness in the conduct of all his business. 2. .bJxercise of due skill and care.- A broker shall act with due skill, care and diligence in the conduct of all his business. 3. Manipulation.- A broker shall not indulge in manipulative, fraudulent or deceptive transactions or schemes or spread rumors with a view to distorting market equilibrium or making personal gains. 4. Malpractices.- A broker shall not create false market either singly or in concert with others or indulge in any act detrimental to the investors' interest or which leads to interference with the fair and smooth functioning of the market. A broker shall not involve himself in excessive speculative business in the market beyond reasonable levels not commensurate with his financial soundness. 5. Compliance with statutory requirements.- A broker shall abide by all the provisions of the Act and the rules, regulations issued by the Commission and the stock exchange from time to time as may be applicable to him. III -107 Brokerslland Agents Reg. Rules, 2001 3rd Schedule B. D y to the Investor 1. E cut ion of orders.- A broker, in his dealings with the clients and the genera investing public, shall faithfully execute the orders for buying and se.llingl f secu~ties at the best available market price and not refuse to. deal WIth a small mvestor merely on the ground of the volume of busmess involve. A broker shall promptly inform his client about the execution or non-ex I cution of an order, and make prompt payment in respect of securities sold an arrange for prompt delivery of securities purchased by clients. 2. Iss e of contract note.- (1) A broker shall not refuse to promptly issue to his lients purchase or sale notes for all the transactions entered into by hi with his clients. (2 A broker shall not refuse to promptly issue to his clients scrip wise lit purchase or sale notes: Pr vided thatan agent shall only split the contract notes client-wise and scripwise originally -issued to him by the affiliated broker into different denominations; and (ii~ an agent shall not match the purchase and sale orders of his clients and each such order must invariably be routed through a I: broker of the stock exchange with whom he is affiliated. 3. Br!aCh of trust.- A broker shall not disclose or discuss with any other person or make improper use of the details of personal investments and other i formation of a confidential nature of a client which he comes to know i his business relationship. 4. Bu iness and commission.- (1) A broker shall no~ encourage sales or purcha es of securities with the sole object of generating brokerage or commi sion. (2) A ~iroker shall not furnish false or misleading quotations or give any ot r false or misleading advice or information to a client with a view of ind cing him to do business in particular securities and enabling himsel to earn brokerage or commission thereby. 5. Bu~ iness of defaulting clients.- A broker shall not deal or transact busine s k~owingly, directly .or indir~ctly or ~xecute.an order fo.r.a cli:llt who ha faIled to carry out hIs commItments ill relatIon to securItIes WIth anothe broker. . 6. Fa rness to clients.- A broker, when dealing with a client, shall disclos whether he is acting as a principal or as an agent and shall ensure at the same time that no conflict of interest arises between him and th I client. In the event of a conflict of interest, he shall inform the client a cordingly and shall not seek to gain a direct or indirect personal advant ge from: the situation and shall not consider clients interest inferior to his own. III- 108 3rd Schedule Company Law and Procedures ~, 7. Investment advice.- A broker shall not make a recommendation to any client who might be expected to rely thereon to acquire, dispose of, retain any securities unless he has reasonable grounds for believing that the recommendation is suitable for such a client upon the basis of the facts, if disclosed by such a client as to his own security holdings, financial situation and objectives of such investment. The broker should seek such information from clients, wherever he feels it is appropriate to do so. 8. Competence of broker.- A broker should have adequately trained staff and arrangements to render fair, prompt and competent services to his clients. C. Broker vis-a-vis other Brokers 1. Conduct of dealings.- A broker shall co-operate with the other contracting party in comparing unmatched transactions. A broker shall not knowingly and wilfully deliver documents which constitute bad delivery and shall co-operate with other contracting party for prompt replacement of documents which are declared as bad delivery. 2. Protection of clients' interest.- A broker shall extend fullest cooperation to other brokers in protecting the interests of his clients regarding their rights to dividends, bonus shares, right shares and any other right related to such securities. 3. Transactions with brokers.- A broker shall carry out his transactions with other brokers and shall comply with his obligations in completing the settlement of transactions with them. 4. Advertisement and publicity.- A broker shall not advertise his business publicly unless permitted by the stock exchange. 5. Inducement of clients.- A broker shall not resort to unfair means of inducing clients from other brokers. 6. False or misleading returns.- A broker shall not neglect or fail or refuse to 'submit the required returns and not make any false or misleading statement on any returns required to be submitted to the Board and to the stock exchange. D. Brokers vis.,.a-vis Commission and Stock Exchange 1. General conduct.- (1) A broker shall not indulge in dishonourable, disgraceful, disorderly or improper conduct on the stock exchange nor shall he wilfully obstruct the business of the stock exchange. He shall comply with the rules, bye-laws and r~gulations of the stock exchange. (2) A broker shall faithfully comply with the general or specific directives issued by the Commission. 2. Failure to give information.- A broker shall not neglect, fail or refuse to submit to the Commission or the stock exchange with which he is registered, such books, special returns, correspondence, documents and papers or any part thereof as may be required. f The Balloters, Transfer Agents and Underwriters Rules, 2001 .Arrangement of Rules Rule 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. THE BALLOTERS, TRANSFER AGENTS AND UNDERWRITERS RULES, 2001 0 472(1)/2001, dated June 27, 2001.- In exercise of the powers confe ed by sectio!l 33 of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 (XVI of 1969), read with clause (b) of section 43 of the Securities and Exch nge Commission of Pakistan Act, 1997 (XLII of 1997), and in purs ance of section 32C of the said Ordinance, the Securities and Exch nge Commission of Pakistan, with the approval of the Federal Gove nment hereby makes the following rules, namely:- ' Short title and commencement.- (1) These rules may be calle the Balloters, Transfer Agents and Underwriters Rules, 2001. Definitions.- (1) In these rules, unless there is anything rep ant in the subject or context,- (a) cc Act" means the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan Act, 1997 (XLII of 1997); (b) "pompany" means a company as defined in the Companies Ordinance, 1984 (XLVII of 1984); (c) "Ordinance" means the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 (XVII of 1969);* .ther~ should have been a full stop instead of semi-colon. R striction on acting as balloter, transfer agent or under writer.- N person shall offer his service, or act as a balloter, transfer agent or n underwriter unless such person fulfils the eligibility conditions pecified in rules 4. 4. C nditions for acting as a balloter, transfer agent or underwri er.- No person shall act as a balloter, transfer agent or underwrite unless such person fulfils the following conditions, namely :- (i) i is a company; (ii)' employs persons possessing managerial experience for ischarging functions offered by it; (iii) .has on its pay roll a person who possesses a degree in law ecognized by the Pakistan Bar Council, or who is a chartered ccountant or a cost and management accountant; (iv) wns computer hardware and software, and employs persons ho are expert in the operation of such hardware and software 0 discharge the services offered; (v) ts directors and employees have not been convicted of an ffence involving fraud or breach of trust; (vi) ts directors and employees have not been punished for an ffence under the Ordinance, the Act any rules made or irective issued thereunder; and (vii) ts directors and employees remain in compliance with the onditions aforesaid or any other requirements notified by the ommission generally or in any particular case. 5. ontractual arrangements mandatory.- (1) A balloter, transfer a ent or underwriter shall not perform services offered by him except pu suant to an agreement in writing that shall state in detail the services t be performed by him and the compensation payable to him for performin the services. (2) he agreement referred to in sub-rule (1) shall contain a provision stating that the arrangement for performing the services or dischargi g the function on behalf of the client and responsibilities which are place on the client, pursuant to the Ordinance or the Act or any other law, for the time being *enforce, does not substitute for, or otherwise diminish, ,he obligation of the client to perform such responsibilities. .should have ~een "in force". ~ 11-21 Balloter~, Transfer Agents, etc. R.7 l- 6. General obligations.- (1) A person working as balloter, transfi r agent or underwriter shall keep. and maintain proper books, record, agreements and documents to show transactions, dealings, receip and transmission of documents, applications and correspondence. (2 The records referred to in sub-rule (1) shall be preserved in good order or a period of not less than five years and shall be open to inspec ion by any person appointed by the Commission for the purpose. (3 A bRlloter, transfer agent or underwriter shall be bound to compl with all general or special dj:!"ectives issued by the Commission. 7. Relaxation of rules.- Where the Commission is satisfied that it is n t practicable '~o comply with any requirement of these rules in a partic lar case or class of cases, the Commission may, for reasons to be record d in writing, relax such requirement subject to suGh conditions as it may deem fit.
